backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with XGBRegressor. Set parameters like max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, and n_estimators=500.
backlog.title: XGBoost implementation

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with LightGBM. Use learning_rate=0.05, number_of_leaves=31, and feature_fraction=0.8.
backlog.title: LightGBM implementation

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with CatBoostRegressor. Set iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, and depth=6.
backlog.title: CatBoost implementation

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaling to the target variable y before training. Use the training set statistics to transform the test set.

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the target variable y if values are strictly positive. This can help normalize variance in clearance data.

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 800 to allow the Random Forest to converge better on the small dataset.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES

backlog.spec: Reduce MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.2 to increase the diversity of the trees by forcing them to sample fewer features.
backlog.title: Decrease MAX_FEATURES

backlog.spec: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 2 to prevent overfitting on the small 970-molecule training set.
backlog.title: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF

backlog.spec: Change RADIUS from 2 to 3 to capture larger structural environments around the atoms.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3

backlog.spec: Modify featurize to use a different fingerprinting method or concatenate Morgan fingerprints with RDKit's Descriptors (e.g., MolWt, LogP).
backlog.title: Add count bits

backlog.spec: Train 3 Random Forests with different seeds and average their predictions.
backlog.title: Ensemble of Random Forests

backlog.spec: Train 3 XGBoost models with different random seeds and average their predictions.
backlog.title: Ensemble of XGBoost

backlog.spec: Implement LightGBM with a validation set (split from train_smiles) and early stopping to find the optimal iteration.
backlog.title: Early stopping for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use sklearn's GradientBoostingRegressor instead of RandomForestRegressor with 300 estimators.
backlog.title: Gradient Boosting Regressor

backlog.spec: Concatenate Morgan fingerprints with a set of 100 basic RDKit descriptors (MolWt, HBD, HBA, etc.) into the final feature vector.
backlog.title: RDKit Descriptors + Morgan

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 to see if a more compressed bitspace improves the signal-to-noise ratio.
backlog.title: Reduce N_BITS

backlog.spec: Replace StandardScaling with RobustScaling to handle potential outliers in the hepatocyte clearance measurements.
backlog.title: RobustScaler

backlog.spec: If using XGBoost/LightGBM, set max_depth to a small value (e.g., 4) to strictly limit model complexity.
backlog.title: Max Depth Constraint

backlog.spec: For LightGBM/XGBoost, implement a simple step decay or exponential decay for the learning rate.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay

backlog.spec: If any RDKit descriptors return NaN, use the median of the training set to fill them.
backlog.title: Median Imputation

backlog.spec: Set max_depth=10 in RandomForestRegressor to bound the complexity of each tree.
backlog.title: Tree Depth limit

backlog.spec: Use a simple variance threshold to remove bits from the Morgan fingerprint that have very low variance across the 970 molecules.
backlog.title: Feature Selection

backlog.spec: Train a Random Forest and an XGBoost model; use a simple weighted average (e.g., 0.7 * RF + 0.3 * XGB) for the prediction.
backlog.title: Weighted Ensemble

backlog.spec: Set max_samples=0.8 in RandomForestRegressor to train each tree on a bootstrap sample of the data.
backlog.title: Subsampling

backlog.spec: Add the Polar Surface Area (PSA) as a separate feature at the end of the featurized array.
backlog.title: Polar Surface Area feature

backlog.spec: Apply np.log2 to the target variable y before training to compress the range of high clearance values.
backlog.title: Log2 Transformation

backlog.spec: When using CatBoost, ensure the featurized numpy array is explicitly cast to float32 or float64 to avoid errors.
backlog.title: CatBoost DTYPE

backlog.spec: Use KFold within fit_predict to perform an internal validation and select the best hyperparameters (like max_depth) for that specific fold.
backlog.title: Cross-Validation Internal Fold

backlog.spec: Predict 1/clearance (intrinsic clearance) instead of clearance directly, as it might be more linear for certain chemical spaces.
backlog.title: Reciprocal Clearance

backlog.spec: Manually implement Z-score normalization (subtract mean, divide by std) on the target y inside fit_predict.
backlog.title: Z-score Normalization

backlog.spec: Replace the ensemble of Random Forest and XGBoost with a LightGBM Regressor. Use 500 estimators, a learning rate of 0.05, and 8 threads. Ensure it uses the same Morgan fingerprint and RDKit descriptors as the current script.
backlog.title: LightGBM Implementation

backlog.spec: Instead of log1p, transform the target y to its ranks (using scipy.stats.rankdata) or a quantile transformation. This can help if the distribution of hepatocyte clearance has outliers that are skewing the correlation.
backlog.title: Rank-based Target Transformation

backlog.spec: Before training, pass the combined feature matrix (Morgan + Descriptors) through sklearn.feature_selection.VarianceThreshold. This will remove descriptors that are nearly constant across the 970 molecules, potentially reducing noise.
backlog.title: Variance Thresholding

backlog.spec: Increase the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3. This captures a larger neighborhood of atoms for each molecule, providing more structural context to the model.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3 Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Create a 3-way ensemble using a 0.4 weight for Random Forest, 0.4 for XGBoost, and 0.2 for LightGBM (or CatBoost). This diversity in tree-building logic might further stabilize the Spearman correlation.
backlog.title: Multi-Model Weighted Ensemble

backlog.spec: Introduce a subsampling step where each fit uses only a random 80% of the available training molecules (re-seeded by the seed argument). This can act as a form of bagging and improve generalization on the held-out skeletons.
backlog.title: Subsampling Training Data

backlog.spec: Modify the XGBoost and LightGBM components to use a decaying learning rate (e.g., exponential decay) instead of a constant learning rate to ensure the model settles into a stable local minimum.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Decay Schedule

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. In some cases, removing the least significant bits of the fingerprint can reduce the dimensionality and noise, potentially improving the signal-to-noise ratio for small datasets.
backlog.title: Reduced Bit Count Morgan

backlog.spec: Add stricter regularization to the XGBoost component: set max_depth=4 and min_child_weight=3. This forces the model to learn more general patterns and prevents it from over-fitting to specific noise in the 970-molecule training set.
backlog.title: Max Depth and Min Child Weight Constraint

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaler to the RDKit Descriptors before concatenating them with the Morgan fingerprints. Currently, descriptors with large numerical ranges might dominate the features of the tree models.
backlog.title: Feature Scaling of Descriptors

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan fingerprint generator to use radius=3. Update the featurizer to handle the larger resulting bit count. This should capture larger local structural contexts of the molecules.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3 Fingerprints

backlog.spec: After featurizing the molecules, calculate the variance of each feature (fingerprint bits and descriptors) across the training set. Remove the bottom 20% of features with the lowest variance before training. This can help reduce noise and improve model focus on discriminative features.
backlog.title: Low-Variance Feature Filtering

backlog.spec: Use the Random Forest model to calculate feature importance. Select the top 50% of features and re-train the ensemble using only these features. This is a more systematic way to prune the feature space than simple variance filtering.
backlog.title: Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE)

backlog.spec: Apply a VarianceThreshold of 0.01 to the concatenated feature matrix (fingerprints + descriptors) to remove constant or near-constant features before passing them to the models.
backlog.title: Variance Thresholding

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 for the Random Forest and set the XGBRegressor's n_estimators to 1000. Since we have a 10-minute time limit, this will test if the bottleneck is model capacity rather than training time.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES for Ensemble Models

backlog.spec: Add regularization parameters to the XGBRegressor: set gamma=0.1 (minimum loss reduction to split) and lambda=1.0 (L2 regularization). This should help stabilize the XGBoost component of the blend.
backlog.title: XGBoost 'gamma' and 'lambda' Regularization

backlog.spec: Create an ensemble of three different Random Forest models, each with a different random_state, and average their predictions. Blend this 'Average RF' with the existing XGBoost model (e.g., 0.5/0.5 split).
backlog.title: Multi-Model Weighted Ensemble with Random Forest

backlog.spec: Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the RDKit descriptors (the last N_DESC features) across the training set. Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation for these features only, before training. Fingerprints should remain as they are.
backlog.title: Standardize RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the log1p transform with a log2 transform: yt = np.log2(y + 1e-6). Use np.expm1 or a custom inverse to return to the original scale. This provides a larger dynamic range for the target values.
backlog.title: Log2 Target Transformation with Exp2

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. This can sometimes reduce noise or prevent overfitting on small datasets by forcing a more compact representation of the molecular features.
backlog.title: Reduce N_BITS for Morgan Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Transform the target variable y to 1/y (or 1/(y+1) to avoid division by zero) before fitting the models. This addresses the characteristic skew of clearance values where large changes in low values are more biologically significant than large changes in high values. Use the appropriate inverse transform for predictions.
backlog.title: Reciprocal Clearance Target

backlog.spec: Standardize the RDKit descriptors (mean 0, variance 1) using the training set statistics before concatenating with the Morgan fingerprints. Since descriptors have widely varying scales (e.g., Molecular Weight vs. LogP), this helps the models (especially those with regularization or gradient descent components) treat them more equitably.
backlog.title: Z-score Standardize RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: Apply scikit-learn's RobustScaler to the concatenated feature vector (Morgan bits + Descriptors). This will scale the features based on percentiles, making the model less sensitive to outliers in the chemical space.
backlog.title: Standardize All Features with RobustScaler

backlog.spec: Add the 'alpha' (L1) and 'lambda' (L2) parameters to the XGBRegressor. Set alpha to a small non-zero value (e.g., 1.0) and lambda to a larger value (e.g., 1.5) to prevent the ensemble from over-fitting to the noisy chemical descriptors.
backlog.title: XGBoost L1 and L2 Regularization

backlog.spec: Add 'max_depth' and 'min_child_weight' to the XGBRegressor. Use a relatively shallow depth (e.g., 5) and a min_child_weight (e.g., 1 to 5) to force the model to find more generalized patterns rather than memorizing specific small molecule skeletons.
backlog.title: Tree Depth and Leaf Weight Constraints

backlog.spec: Set 'subsample' to 0.7 and 'colsample_bytree' to 0.7 in the XGBRegressor. This introduces stochasticity by training each tree on a different subset of the data and features, which often improves generalization in chemical property prediction.
backlog.title: XGBoost subsample and colsample_bytree

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES to 1000 for both the RandomForestRegressor and the XGBRegressor. Since the dataset is small (970 molecules) and we have 8 threads, increasing the number of trees may help smooth the prediction surface without significantly impacting the time limit.
backlog.title: Increase Ensemble Model Trees

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBRegressor with a LightGBMRegressor. Implement early stopping by using a validation set split within the fit_predict call to find the optimal number of iterations, preventing the model from over-fitting the 970 samples.
backlog.title: LightGBM with Early Stopping

backlog.spec: Create a 3-way ensemble using RandomForestRegressor, XGBRegressor, and LightGBMRegressor. Use a weighted average (e.g., 0.33 each or optimized weights) to combine their predictions. This diversity of boosting and bagging techniques often produces a more robust variance-bias tradeoff.
backlog.title: Multi-Model Weighted Ensemble (RF, XGB, LightGBM)

backlog.spec: Implement a learning rate decay schedule for XGBRegressor. Instead of a constant learning_rate, use a small initial rate (e.g., 0.01) and manually train for more iterations or use the 'learning_rate' parameter in conjunction with a higher number of estimators to allow the model to converge more slowly and stably.
backlog.title: XGBoost Learning Rate Decay

backlog.spec: The current script concatenates raw RDKit descriptors with Morgan fingerprints. Since descriptors like TPSA and various molecular weights can have vastly different scales, use scikit-learn's RobustScaler to standardize the RDKit descriptor portion of the feature vector (the last 100 columns) before concatenating them with the binary fingerprints. This should help the tree models handle the varying magnitudes of the physical properties more effectively.
backlog.title: Standardize RDKit Descriptors with RobustScaler

backlog.spec: Instead of predicting the clearance value directly (or its log), try predicting the reciprocal of the clearance (1 / clearance). In pharmacokinetic modeling, clearance values are often skewed; taking the reciprocal can sometimes linearize the relationship between chemical structure and clearance, potentially making it easier for the ensemble to capture the underlying variance. If this is used, the final prediction should be inverted back to the original clearance scale.
backlog.title: Reciprocal Clearance Target

backlog.spec: Instead of the RF/XGB ensemble, replace the Random Forest component with an average of three separate RandomForestRegressor instances, each using a different random seed. This is based on the observation that a 3-way RF average performed well in previous explorations. Use the same hyperparameters (N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF) for all three.
backlog.title: Ensemble of three Random Forests

backlog.spec: Instead of taking only the first 100 RDKit descriptors (N_DESC = 100), use all available descriptors provided by the Descriptors.descList. This will significantly increase the feature dimensionality but may provide more comprehensive information about the molecules' physical and chemical properties.
backlog.title: Full RDKit Descriptor Set

backlog.spec: Add regularization parameters to the XGBRegressor component of the ensemble. Specifically, set 'reg_alpha' (L1 regularization) to 1.0 and 'reg_lambda' (L2 regularization) to 1.0. This is intended to prevent the XGBoost component from overfitting to noise in the small dataset of 970 molecules.
backlog.title: XGBoost L1 and L2 Regularization

backlog.spec: Apply scikit-learn's StandardScaler to the entire feature set (Morgan fingerprints + RDKit descriptors) before feeding them into the models. While tree-based models are generally invariant to monotonic transformations, standardizing features can sometimes improve training stability and convergence behavior for ensemble methods like XGBoost.
backlog.title: Z-score Standardize All Features

backlog.spec: Reduce the N_BITS parameter from 2048 to 1024. By reducing the dimensionality of the Morgan fingerprints, you may reduce the risk of the models memorizing noise in the sparse bit space, potentially improving generalization on the unseen skeletons in the test folds.
backlog.title: Reduce Morgan Fingerprint Bits to 1024

backlog.spec: Increase the number of trees for both the Random Forest (N_TREES) and the XGBoost (n_estimators) components. Try setting N_TREES to 600 and XGBoost n_estimators to 800. More trees should reduce the variance of the ensemble's predictions, provided the 10-minute time limit allows for it.
backlog.title: Increase Ensemble Model Trees

backlog.spec: Add the 'gamma' parameter to the XGBRegressor with a value of 1.0. This represents the minimum loss reduction required to make a split. Combined with 'reg_lambda' (L2 regularization), this provides a stronger mechanism to control the complexity of the XGBoost trees and prevent them from becoming too deep or complex.
backlog.title: XGBoost 'gamma' and 'lambda' Tuning

backlog.spec: Transform the target variable to be the relative clearance (y / median(y)). This is a bold data transformation that centers the target around 1.0. It might help the models learn the relative magnitude of clearance more effectively across different molecular classes. The final prediction would be multiplied back by the median of the training set values.
backlog.title: Relative Clearance Difference

backlog.spec: In the `featurize` function, expand the feature vector by adding 166 bits from `MACCSKeys` and the 20 fragment descriptors from `CrippenDescriptor` (calculated via `rdkit.Chem.descriptors.CrippenDescriptor`). Concatenate these with the existing Morgan fingerprint and RDKit descriptors.
backlog.title: Add MACCS Keys and Crippen fragment descriptors

backlog.spec: In the `featurize` function, include the `AtomPairFingerprint` (using `rdkit.Chem.AllChem.GetAtomPairFingerprint`) and `TopologicalTorsions` (using `rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.CalcTopologicalTorsionCount`) as additional features to capture larger structural arrangements.
backlog.title: Add Atom Pair and Topological Torsion counts

backlog.spec: Increase `N_TREES` to 1000 for the RandomForestRegressor and the XGBRegressor `n_estimators` to 1000. This increases model capacity to capture more complex patterns at the cost of training time.
backlog.title: Increase ensemble tree counts for RF and XGB

backlog.spec: Before training, apply `sklearn.preprocessing.RobustScaler` to the descriptor portion of the feature matrix. This handles outliers in the RDKit descriptors more effectively than simple clipping or log transforms.
backlog.title: Robust Scaling for all descriptors

backlog.spec: While the harness doesn't easily support callbacks, simulate a better schedule by reducing the `learning_rate` of the XGBRegressor to 0.01 and increasing `n_estimators` to 2000, which is a common way to achieve more stable convergence in the absence of early stopping.
backlog.title: Add Early Stopping to XGBoost (via iteration counts)

backlog.spec: Use `sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler` to scale the RDKit descriptors (but not the binary Morgan bits) to zero mean and unit variance. This ensures that descriptors with large units do not dominate the gradient in the XGBoost model.
backlog.title: Standardize descriptors with Z-score

backlog.spec: Introduce `lightgbm.LGBMRegressor` as a third component in the blend. Train it with 500 estimators and a learning rate of 0.05. Update the prediction to be a weighted average of the three models (e.g., 0.3 RF, 0.3 XGB, 0.4 LightGBM).
backlog.title: Weighted Ensemble with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Before fitting the final models, use a preliminary `RandomForestRegressor` to rank the importance of all features (fingerprints + descriptors) and discard the bottom 25% of features to reduce noise and dimensionality.
backlog.title: Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) on descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the `np.log1p` transform with `np.log2` and the `np.expm1` inverse with `np.exp2` (or `2**pred`). This can sometimes provide a more linear mapping for clearance values that span several orders of magnitude.
backlog.title: Log2 Target Transform with Exp2 Inverse

backlog.spec: Calculate weights for the `train_y` based on the inverse of the target values (i.e., `weights = 1 / (y + 1)`). Use these weights during the `fit` method of the RandomForestRegressor (if supported) or use them to scale the targets during training to prioritize low-clearance molecules.
backlog.title: Custom Weighting for Target Values

incumbent.description: Set N_DESC to len(Descriptors.descList) so the featurizer uses every RDKit descriptor instead of the first 100, leaving the rest of train.py unchanged.

memo: Helped: data and target changes. Adding 100 RDKit descriptors to Morgan bits gave 0.5829 (from 0.6103). The log1p target gave 0.5592. The 0.7/0.3 RF+XGBoost blend gave 0.5422/0.5380. The biggest recent gain was using all RDKit descriptors (slot 29, 0.5159), which is the incumbent. Did not help: family swaps (CatBoost 0.5755, LightGBM 0.5677, GBR 0.5548), regularization (XGB L1/L2 0.5203, depth 4 0.5444, subsample/colsample 0.7 0.5452), Morgan radius 3 (0.5492), 1024 bits (0.5174), and variance-based feature pruning (0.5159, no change). Micro-tweaks stayed within the 0.0070 noise sd. Next: add other feature types on top of the full descriptor set, such as MACCS keys, atom-pair or topological-torsion counts, and Crippen/EState fragment descriptors. Then retry the 3-way RF/XGB/LightGBM blend (0.5355-0.5360 earlier, unreplicated) on the new features. Avoid more family swaps, radius changes and micro-tweaks.
